title: What the Archive Consciousness Engine is
description: The engine maintains a continuously updated operational model of every archive it can reach. For each archive it records contents, schema, relationships to other archives, known limitations, and demonstrated capabilities. When a question arrives, the engine consults the model first and routes work to the archives actually able to answer, instead of searching blindly.

title: Archive descriptor schema
description: Every archive is described by the same machine-readable schema: identity, holdings summary, schema version, update cadence, access permissions, known gaps, and measured capability scores. The schema is what makes archives comparable — without it, the engine would be comparing marketing copy instead of operational facts.

title: Archive health scoring algorithm
description: The engine scores each archive's health from observable signals: descriptor freshness, query success rate, result completeness, and schema drift. A archive that answers quickly but with stale data scores worse than a slower archive with fresh verified holdings. The score is recomputed continuously and drives routing decisions.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Archive health scoring algorithm

architecture: Signal collectors feed a scoring function with fixed weights; scores decay with descriptor age; the routing layer sorts candidate archives by score before dispatching any query.

title: Change detection across archive snapshots
description: Watchers take periodic snapshots of each archive's descriptor and holdings summary, then diff them to detect real change: new collections, removed datasets, schema migrations, permission changes. Change events update the operational model and alert downstream tools that cached assumptions may be wrong.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Change detection across archive snapshots

architecture: Snapshots are content-hashed and stored in a ring buffer; a differ computes semantic change sets (added/removed/changed) rather than raw byte diffs; events publish to a change bus.

title: Ingestion: archive watcher adapters
description: Archives expose themselves differently — some publish DCAT feeds, some have crawlable catalogs, some only answer queries. Watcher adapters normalize each style into descriptors: feed adapters poll on schedule, crawl adapters walk catalogs, probe adapters infer capabilities from sampled queries. Every adapter reports its own confidence.

title: Capability index and fast lookup
description: The operational model is indexed for millisecond capability questions: an inverted index from capability terms to archives, a spatial index over freshness, and a permission lattice for access filtering. The index is rebuilt incrementally as descriptors change so routing never waits on a full rebuild.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Capability index and fast lookup

architecture: In-memory inverted index plus persistent snapshot; incremental updates applied per descriptor change; read replicas serve the query API while the writer applies updates.

title: Limitation inference: what archives cannot do
description: Knowing what an archive cannot do is as valuable as knowing what it can. The engine infers limitations from negative evidence: repeated query failures, schema gaps, permission denials, and explicit limitation statements in descriptors. Limitations are stored as first-class facts so the router can explain why an archive was skipped.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Limitation inference: what archives cannot do

architecture: A limitation store keyed by (archive, capability) with evidence lists; inference rules promote repeated failures into stated limitations; the router consults limitations before candidates.

description: The engine benchmarks itself against reality: it samples archives directly, measures actual freshness and latency, and compares those measurements with what the model predicted. title: Failure modes: stale models and silent archives
description: The engine's own failure modes are documented and measured: descriptors that go stale when watchers fail, archives that change without notice, and confidence scores that drift from reality. Each failure mode has a detector and a fallback — when the model is uncertain, it says so and probes the archive directly instead of guessing.

title: Scaling: sharded consciousness across regions
description: One engine cannot watch every archive on the planet from one machine. The design shards by archive geography and topic: regional engines maintain local models and federate capability queries upward. A query fans out, regional models answer from their shard, and the top level merges rankings.

architecture: Regional model shards with a federation root; gossip protocol keeps shard summaries synchronized; queries fan out with timeouts and merge partial rankings deterministically.

title: Security: permission-aware operational model
description: The model itself is sensitive: knowing exactly what an archive holds can leak information. Descriptors carry permission scopes, the query API filters by caller identity, and the engine never reveals holdings a caller is not allowed to see. Audit logs record every capability query and what was disclosed.

demo.title: Runnable code demo — Security: permission-aware operational model

architecture: Identity-aware query layer; permission lattice evaluated per request; audit log append-only; descriptor fields tagged with visibility levels.

title: Compounded integration and acceptance suite
description: The full engine is accepted only when the loop closes: watchers feed descriptors, the model updates, queries route correctly, benchmarks match the model, and failures are detected. The acceptance suite runs the whole loop against a fixture of synthetic archives and requires every stage to pass before the build is called operational.
